---
title: "Pairwise errors from joint posterior draws"
subtitle: "4.11 · after postrank’s posterior-input vignettes"
description: "Pairing values from different posterior draws can change the estimated direction errors."
---

A posterior draw gives the values of all units and criteria in one joint state. We estimate the probability of
a wrong direction by counting the states in which it is wrong and dividing by the number of draws. The package's
32-state example shows what happens if we shift the values for one unit by a row. The unit has the same
marginal values, but the shift changes which values it is compared with. Shifting all units together
reorders complete states and preserves the full-sample error rates.

```{=html}
<div id="app" class="prx-app column-page"></div>

<script src="../../js/vendor/plot.min.js"></script>
```

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Original states.** Among the 32 retained states, placing 001 above site-B is wrong 8 times on need_A and
  32 times on need_B. The empirical error shares are .250 and 1. Each complete state specifies the order of all three units on both criteria.
- **Shift one unit.** Moving site-B’s whole two-criterion vector forward cyclically changes the need_A count to
  7 times and its share to .219. The need_B count remains 32 times. The raw marginal values have only been
  reordered; the joint pairing has changed.
- **Move states together.** Applying the same shift to every unit restores the original full-sample counts:
  8 times and 32 times. Each state still contains the same values, so every full-sample error share stays the same.
- **Short prefix.** Only 8 retained states now enter the estimates. Even a shift of complete states can change which draws appear in the first 8 rows.
- **Unshifted pair.** The pair 001 and site C contains neither shifted unit. Its counts remain 0 times and
  25 times, with need_B share .781. Changing a third unit’s pairing cannot change this pair’s comparisons.
- **Full cycle.** A full cyclic shift returns every source vector to its original row, with counts 8 times and
  32 times again. The source table retains all original unit and criterion coordinates.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The original states are independent draws from the same synthetic normal law. An error share of zero means that
no retained draw shows the event. Its posterior probability can still be positive. The shifted comparisons reuse
the original sample to show how pairing across units affects the estimated probabilities.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
```r
library(postrank)
e <- postrank_pairwise(postrank_toy)$e
e["001", "site-B", ]  # need_A .25, need_B 1
```
:::
